question: A migraineur who takes analgesics (paracetamol, NSAIDs, or triptans) on ≥10–15 days per month for more than 3 months is at risk of medication-overuse headache, and the treatment is withdrawal of the overused medication.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. MOH is the most common cause of chronic daily headache (>15 headache days/month). It is caused by overuse of acute headache medications. The key treatment is medication withdrawal — adding more analgesics worsens the cycle. Always counsel migraine patients about this risk.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Medication-overuse headache (MOH, formerly 'analgesic rebound headache') develops when analgesics are used too frequently. Triptans/ergotamines → MOH at ≥10 days/month; simple analgesics (paracetamol, NSAIDs) → MOH at ≥15 days/month. Treatment is abrupt or gradual withdrawal of the overused agent, with bridging therapy (prednisolone taper or naproxen) and initiation of preventive therapy.
